newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Central Bank adjusts T-bill rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Central Bank adjusts T-bill rates.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Tuesday it lowered its borrowing rate on its 85-day special series Treasury bill rate to 10.575 percent from 10.65.
But the Central Bank raised its rate on the 162-day bill to 10.80 percent from 10.65.
Dealers said the Central Bank merely aligned its rates with Monday's results of the primary auction of Treasury bills.
The bellwether 91-day T-bill rate slipped to an average of 10.673 percent on Monday from the previous week's 10.727 while the other maturities rose.
Traders said the mixed direction of rates reflected the market's view that rates had bottomed out and had started to move upwards.

The Central Bank also stopped offering on Tuesday reverse repos with a term of four days after selling such bills last Thursday. Reverse repos with a term of less than six days are not subject to the 20 percent tax.
